stories.title: Trump now says he wants to form an ‘AI Force’
stories.simple_summary: The president announced plans to create a new government group called an 'AI Force' and appoint a leader to oversee artificial intelligence development. This comes as many people worry that AI is growing too fast without enough safety checks.
stories.why_it_matters: This might eventually affect how AI companies operate in the US, but for now it's mostly political news — no immediate changes for you.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang rejects AI extinction warnings as "doomsday narratives"
stories.simple_summary: An important leader at Nvidia said that warnings about AI becoming too dangerous are overblown and exaggerated.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who worry about AI safety — nothing that changes your daily life right now.

stories.title: Trump to host China's Xi Jinping for trade, AI talks
stories.simple_summary: The president plans to meet with China's leader to discuss trade and artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political negotiation news — nothing you need to act on, though international AI policies could eventually affect tech prices.

stories.title: Hackers who broke into OpenAI warn the AI industry has a security problem
stories.simple_summary: Computer hackers broke into OpenAI and are warning that the AI industry doesn't protect its systems well enough from attacks.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that AI companies need better security, like how a shop needs better locks — relevant if you use AI tools, but most people shouldn't panic.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang on artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: An Nvidia leader gave comments or statements about artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This is too vague from the headline to explain what was actually said — nothing to worry about without more details.

stories.title: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems
stories.simple_summary: Power plants and electricity systems are still mostly hacked by actual people, not by AI running wild on its own. The real danger comes from regular cybercriminals, not killer robots.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business that uses electricity (which is all of them), it's good to know the real threats are from human hackers, so normal security practices still matter most.

stories.title: Jensen Huang says there is '0% chance' AI destroys the world by 2030 — 'We should go as fast as we can, irrespective of anyone else,' dismisses Anthropic doom warnings and rejects new regulations
stories.simple_summary: A Nvidia leader said he's confident AI won't destroy the world by 2030 and that companies should develop AI as fast as possible without waiting for new rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people worried about AI safety — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: China’s A.I. Makes a Great Leap Forward. But Its Economy Is Falling Behind.
stories.simple_summary: China is making good progress with its own AI technology, but its economy is still struggling overall.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly international business and economics news — it may eventually affect global tech prices, but nothing urgent for you now.

stories.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
stories.simple_summary: The president announced plans to create an 'AI Force' government group and hire someone to lead it and oversee AI technology.
stories.why_it_matters: Same as headline 0 — this is political news about future plans, nothing that immediately affects you.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
stories.simple_summary: Meta created an AI assistant called Muse that can read your messages, calendar, and notes on Apple computers, and it works well but feels creepy because it's so intrusive.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Meta products on a Mac, be aware this AI can access your personal information — think of it like hiring someone who gets to read all your mail and your calendar.

stories.title: Flock reportedly tries to shrink workforce with employee buyouts
stories.simple_summary: A company called Flock is offering employees money to leave their jobs instead of doing full layoffs.
stories.why_it_matters: This is company news — mostly relevant only if you work at Flock or care about that specific business.

stories.title: Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow
stories.simple_summary: The president plans to create an 'AI Force' government group to monitor and oversee AI technology as concerns grow that AI systems are becoming too independent and hard to control.
stories.why_it_matters: Same as headlines 0 and 8 — this is political planning news, nothing urgent for you to do right now.
